title: Verify A Tracked Edit With Changes And Dump Runs
task: Create an edited output document in the run directory using docxedit only.

Start with docxedit changes --json on the private input copy, then use read, context, find, or dump with low text limits to choose a small visible paragraph target that appears free of existing tracked-change, comment, field, hyperlink, drawing, or semantic-anchor boundaries.
Create a .docxpatch for a small replace-text edit with expect-text, or a small insert-after edit if replacement is not safe.
Run docxedit check before apply using --track-changes require, --author "DocxEdit Challenge", and --timestamp-utc "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z".
Apply to a separate output .docx under the run directory with the same track-change options.
Verify the output with docxedit changes --json and docxedit dump --runs --view markup --json on the edited target.
In the final response, report command classes, target IDs, diagnostic codes, change types, run markup types, and artifact filenames only; do not quote private document text.
successCriteria: Uses changes --json before and after the edit.
Uses dump --runs --view markup on the edited output target.
Uses check before apply with --track-changes require.
Produces an output .docx if a safe target exists, or stops with the relevant diagnostics if require-mode tracking cannot be represented.
Does not inspect raw OOXML package parts or quote private document text.
observerQuestions: Could the agent discover a safe tracked-edit target without document-specific hints?
Did it understand that changes IDs and dump run IDs are different namespaces?
Did dump --runs expose enough inserted/deleted run metadata to verify the edit?
Did the agent avoid falling back to direct edits when require-mode tracking failed?
Were any docxedit commands confusing enough to cause retries or malformed patches?
